title: Loops
description: While loops, for loops, range(), and break

exercises.title: The While Loop
exercises.content: A 'while' loop keeps running a block of code as long as its condition is True. Each time through the loop, Python checks the condition again. If it's still True, the code runs again. If it's False, the loop stops and Python moves on.
exercises.code:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print(count)
    count = count + 1

highlights.note: The 'while' keyword checks this condition before each loop. If True, run the indented code. If False, stop.
This line changes 'count' so that eventually the condition becomes False. Without it, the loop would run forever!

exercises.title: The For Loop
exercises.content: A 'for' loop runs code once for each item in a sequence. The variable after 'for' takes on each value, one at a time. This is perfect when you know exactly what values you want to loop through.

highlights.note: A list of items to loop through.
'for fruit in fruits' means: for each item in the list, call it 'fruit' and run the indented code.
This runs 3 times — once for each fruit in the list.

exercises.title: Watch: For Loop (List)

exercises.title: Range()
exercises.content: The range() function generates a sequence of numbers. range(5) gives you 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — it starts at 0 and stops BEFORE the number you give it. You can also give it a start: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2, 3.

highlights.note: range(5) generates: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. It always starts at 0 and stops BEFORE 5.
range(2, 5) generates: 2, 3, 4. Starts at 2, stops BEFORE 5.

exercises.title: Watch: Accumulator Pattern
exercises.code:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total = total + i
print(total)

exercises.question: What numbers does range(2, 6) give you?

Use a for loop with range() to print the numbers 1 through 5

codeTests.message: Use range(5) to get numbers 0-5 (and add 1) or range(1, 6) to get numbers 1-5

exercises.title: Break
exercises.content: Sometimes you want to stop a loop early. The 'break' keyword immediately exits the loop — Python jumps to the first line after the loop. This is useful when you're searching for something and want to stop as soon as you find it.

highlights.note: When num equals 3, 'break' stops the loop immediately. We never get to print 3, 4, or 5.
After break, Python continues here — the first line after the loop.
